summary.intent: Back up all openclaw data, code, and config from a remote VPS (76.13.137.104) to a local folder before decommissioning the server. Then resolve open CodeRabbit review comments on a CipherBox PR.
summary.outcome: Full consistent openclaw snapshot (2.1 GB, 155,622 files) transferred and SHA-256 verified at ~/Code/random/openclaw-backup/. VPS services left stopped for retirement. BACKLOG.md 'uint8ToBase64 copies' count corrected from '4-5' to '3'; commit pending 1Password signing approval.

repo: CodeRabbit posts nitpicks in the review body, not as inline threads — unresolved thread count will always show 0; must fetch review bodies separately to find actionable feedback
BACKLOG.md:53 had a stale count ('4-5 copies') for uint8ToBase64; the canonical count in TECH_DEBT-v1.1.md (3 copies) matched actual codebase grep results
uint8ToBase64 has 3 copies: sdk-core/file, sdk-core/folder, and web/file-metadata.service

commit.gpgsign=true with op-ssh-sign (1Password) signer — signed commits hang waiting for 1Password UI approval; must run unsandboxed in background with a long timeout and manually approve the 1Password prompt

code.finding: Count of uint8ToBase64 duplicate copies was '4-5'; corrected to '3' to match TECH_DEBT-v1.1.md and grep results

workflow: SSH on public VPS IP was firewalled; Tailscale (openclaw-hostinger, 100.118.33.115) was the correct access path — always check Tailscale first when public SSH is blocked

1Password SSH agent (SSH_AUTH_SOCK → ~/Library/Group Containers/2BUA8C4S2C.com.1password/t/agent.sock) was already live and serving the VPS key — writing a temp key file to disk was unnecessary and left the private key in session transcript logs
For consistent backups of stateful processes, stop services before tarring — live snapshots of ~/.openclaw type data risk partial writes
pigz (parallel gzip) available on the VPS enables faster compression on multi-core hosts
Background scp progress can be monitored by polling local file size; ~2 MB/s was the bottleneck on VPS upstream bandwidth, not the Tailscale tunnel
Always remove temp SSH key files only after the scp process has fully exited, not before — scp loads the key at connection start but may still reference the path

friction: SSH on public IP (76.13.137.104) was completely firewalled — every port filtered — requiring a pivot to Tailscale, which wasn't discovered until after probing network and checking 1Password items

Private key was written to disk as a temp file AND appeared in plaintext in session transcript logs during initial 1Password item inspection (field type SSHKEY not CONCEALED) — a security gap for a root key
git commit with 1Password signing hung and was killed by timeout (45s) — required retry as unsandboxed background task with manual 1Password approval prompt
User requested services be stopped for consistent snapshot after the live tar was already in progress, requiring abort and restart of the build job
Background task polling produced no output initially, creating ambiguity about build progress
open_items: BACKLOG.md fix commit (signed) is pending 1Password approval — needs user to approve the 1Password prompt, then push and resolve the CodeRabbit thread
CodeRabbit review body finding on PR #515 has not yet been replied to or resolved — requires gh api calls after commit lands
Tarball contains live secrets (root/.git-credentials, root/.op-token, browser profile cookies) — needs secure storage, not committed anywhere
VPS root private key appeared in plaintext in session transcript logs — moot once VPS is nuked, but rotate from any other host's authorized_keys if the key was reused
~/.ssh (authorized_keys/known_hosts), /home/ubuntu, root crontab, and /etc system config were not included in the backup — acceptable if openclaw was the only workload, but not verified
